articles.title: The Duskbloods Playtest Was Even More Popular Than Elden Ring Nightreign’s
articles.summary: It sounds like fans were eager to learn everything they could about From Software's The Duskbloods, as one of the game's producers has revealed the Switch 2 exclusive saw higher playtest sign-ups compared to Elden Ring Nightreign.
body: Speaking during a livestream hosted by Japanese gaming publication Famitsu (and translated by GamesRadar+ ), From Software producer Yasuhiro Kitao stated the number of applications for The Duskbloods playtest eclipsed that of the developer's previous multiplayer experiment.

Given that Elden Ring Nightreign's playtest was available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S (the full game was also available on PC and last-gen consoles) the fact that The Duskbloods received more interest on Switch 2 sounds like it should be impossible. The Switch 2 is also a relatively new console, having only been available for around a year, meaning its user base is much smaller compared to that of the other two consoles.

While it is surprising on the surface, perhaps there is some logic to be deciphered here. Elden Ring Nightreign went on to sell more than 5 million copies, with its DLC alone selling 2 million copies in under a week. The game's popularity and success proved From Software could make a wildly fun, multiplayer-focused souls-like, perhaps generating more interest for The Duskbloods.

articles.title: Amazon and Twitch Face Class Action Lawsuit After Introducing Opt-Out Setting That Uses Streamers' Content to Train AI
articles.summary: Twitch and Amazon are facing a class-action lawsuit after the streaming platform rolled out a feature that automatically trains its generative AI on streamers’ content unless they manually opt out. The setting sparked a wave of backlash when it was rolled out last week.
body: It’s buried in users’ security and privacy settings, and is automatically turned on by default. Streamers must toggle the option off in order to opt out of it — but that doesn’t stop Twitch from using their channel content for other purposes, as outlined in the platform’s Privacy Notice.

“Defendants’ actions were not only unlawful, but an unconscionable attack on the community of content creators whose content is used to fuel the multitrillion-dollar generative AI industry without any compensation," the suit reads.

"Content creators such as Plaintiff and the Class Members will never be able to claw back the intellectual property unlawfully copied and used by Defendants to train Amazon’s generative AI. Once AI ingests content, that content is stored in its neural network, and not capable of deletion or retraction. Defendants’ actions constitute abuse and exploitation of content creators’ work for Defendants’ profit."

Damages sought include “all available contract damages, including actual, compensatory, consequential, and nominal damages, together with such other relief as the Court deems just and proper,” though no specific monetary amount was mentioned.
points: Twitch and Amazon are facing a class-action lawsuit after the streaming platform rolled out a feature that automatically trains its generative AI on streamers’ content unless they manually opt out.

articles.title: I Can’t Believe I Missed Mortal Shell 2’s Best Item, Silly Me
articles.summary: From awesome Tarstones to exceptional weapons, there are a lot of really good items to find in Mortal Shell 2. While you can miss them if you're not doing your due diligence while exploring, there's an early-game item that you really don't want to miss because of how it trivializes most fights.
body: The first boss you fight happens in the prologue. After some light exploration and acquiring your first shell, Haros, you roll up on the Tar Golem, who absolutely wrecks your stuff. It's designed as a forced loss, so actually putting up a fight is pointless, especially since a cutscene plays showing that Haros saves your life anyway.

It's here that you loot your now-dead shell for the Vatra's Seal, which hardens your body to nullify incoming damage and freezes you mid-animation. It's actually a pretty overpowered seal. Not only does it cancel out damage, causing enemies to get knocked back if they attack your shell, but it also acts as an animation cancel, letting you interrupt your attacks by hardening your body to guard. Time the harden just right and you've got a perfect parry, which deals massive posture damage and eventually leads to a counterattack.

Vatra's Seal is essentially the main ability from the first Mortal Shell. But instead of it being tied to one specific shell, when you loot Haros' corpse in the sequel, you can harden your body no matter which shell you currently have equipped. It rules.
points: From awesome Tarstones to exceptional weapons, there are a lot of really good items to find in Mortal Shell 2.
While you can miss them if you're not doing your due diligence while exploring, there's an early-game item that you really don't want to miss because of how it trivializes most fights.

articles.title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Is Way Ahead Of Black Ops 7 Already By One Metric
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is nearing 400,000 copies sold on Steam already, and that's well ahead of where last year's Black Ops 7 stood at launch on Valve's platform.
body: Elliott said Black Ops 7 managed to hit around 200,000 copies pre-sold on Steam by launch. Modern Warfare 4 has doubled that, and with two months still to go before release.

MW4's beta put up big numbers on Steam during its early-access period, reaching a peak of more than 115,000 concurrent users. Black Ops 7, meanwhile, peaked at about 100,000 concurrent users on Steam, even after it went live for everyone outside of a beta weekend, according to ChalieIntel.

MW4 performing better than Black Ops 7 by some metrics already is not a total surprise, as last year's game was a commercial disappointment. In fact, its sales ranking in the US was the lowest for the series since 2008.

The next MW4 beta is coming up this weekend, running August 28-September 1. This will be an open beta, so anyone on any platform can play without needing to preorder. Additionally, this beta will extend to Nintendo Switch 2.

articles.title: Buddy Review
articles.summary: Review: Buddy sees Too Many Cooks director Casper Kelly overcome some significant pacing hitches to deliver a singular horror-comedy that delights in subverting the treacly sweetness of kids’ TV with lots of sticky blood and a smart take on some heavier themes.
body: Buddy wastes no time revealing its central conceit and how it plans to push that forward. One of the kids tires of Buddy pretty much immediately, and the fallout of that slight attracts the curiosity of Freddy (Delaney Quinn), another kid in Buddy’s thrall. Quinn’s performance, like Key’s, is impressive in its control, never getting ahead of where Kelly has pitched the tone at any given point. The rest of the kids who make up Buddy’s gang get the occasional chance to shine, but Freddy’s the only one who really has space to develop her character past a caricature of “kid with fewer lines than the others in an episode of Barney.”

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaks: A Timeline Of The Events So Far
articles.summary: It's been a busy few weeks for Rockstar and Take-Two following a series of leaked GTA 6 gameplay videos and images. Beginning in mid-August 2026, an anonymous individual or group calling itself CyberLeek began publishing unreleased Grand Theft Auto 6 material.
body: The situation is still unfolding, so we've got a roundup of all of the events of the most recent GTA 6 leak in chronological order, along with what the footage appears to show, and CyberLeek's communications so far. Ahead of the footage being posted more widely, several Reddit users believe that infrastructure including the main CyberLeek domain and backup spelling variants were registered as early as August 14. They also claim that a $CYBERLEEK token, liquidity pool, website, and voting program were created around August 15.

The first clip was around a minute long, and showed protagonist Jason Duval outside the oceanside house that's already been seen in official Rockstar marketing material. It showed off a Focus mechanic, where making a basket increased Jason's Focus level, as shown on the HUD. It's unclear whether this Focus system is present across all of the gameplay, or only in minigames such as basketball. It was initially unclear whether the footage was genuine, but as Rockstar begin issuing DMCA takedown notices, it appeared to verify the legitimacy.

articles.title: Vampire Hunter D Returns: The Cult-Classic Horror Series Finds New Life in 2026
articles.summary: Vampire Hunter D is a franchise that has enjoyed a long, healthy lifespan as a series of Japanese light novels, but has never really been explored to its fullest in other media. The last Vampire Hunter D film to be released was 2001's Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust.
body: First up, Dark Horse Comics is releasing a new miniseries called Vampire Hunter D: Fortress of Blood. The series isn't an adaptation of one of Hideyuki Kikuchi's novels, but is rather an original story set in that post-apocalyptic universe. Fortress of Blood is written by Chris Condon (That Texas Blood) and illustrated by Filipe Andrade (The Many Deaths of Laila Starr).
Vampire Hunter D: Fortress of Blood #1 will be released on December 16. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop.
On the film front, GKIDS revealed that Bloodlust is getting a theatrical rerelease in 2027, just after the film's 25th anniversary.

There are no further details regarding a release date or possible 4k Blu-ray release, but hopefully Bloodlust returning to theaters will spark new interest in the series and pave the way for another film or anime series. Previously, an anime called Vampire Hunter D: Resurrection was announced in 2015, but work on the series seemingly stalled out during the COVID-19 pandemic.

articles.title: Tom Hardy’s $478M Sci-Fi Action Movie Officially Surges to #2 on Netflix
articles.summary: Over the years, Tom Hardy has proven to be one of the most versatile actors around. He's starred in Oscar-winning dramas like Alejandro Iñárritu's The Revenant and led blockbuster smash hits like Mad Max: Fury Road.
body: Fresh off the success of Spider-Man: Homecoming, Sony launched its own Spider-Man Universe in 2018 with Venom. Tom Hardy was cast in the dual lead roles of Eddie Brock and Venom (previously portrayed by Topher Grace in Sam Rami’s Spider-Man 3 ). The prospect of a movie about a Spider-Man villain that didn't include Spider-Man was a weird pitch, and Hardy delivered an equally unconventional performance to match. It's that charming commitment to the role that made Venom a cult hit.

Fans especially latched onto the romantic side of Eddie and Venom's relationship, which 2021's Venom: Let There Be Carnage would lean into. While Sony's other Spider-Man Universe films like Morbius and Madame Web crashed and burned, becoming fodder for endless memes, Venom persisted. In 2024, Hardy returned for Venom: The Last Dance, which is now the second-most streamed movie on Netflix.

articles.title: 38 Years Later, The Best 'Calvin and Hobbes' Mom Quote Is Still Unmatched in Comic Strip History
articles.summary: Calvin’s mom doesn't get enough credit. Within Bill Watterson’s classic comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Calvin’s mom, who is a homemaker, is Calvin’s number one nurturer and the person preparing nearly all of his meals (which Calvin definitely doesn’t appreciate).
body: There’s a ton of love for Calvin’s dad. People love that, just for his own amusement, Calvin's dad will make up absurd lies, like when Calvin asks his dad where babies come from, only for his dad to say “Most people just go to Sears, buy the kit, and follow the assembly instructions.” But Calvin’s mom — who, like Calvin’s dad, has no name — doesn’t get nearly as much love. Even Watterson himself has admitted that he underserved the character.

“Calvin's mom is the daily disciplinarian, a job that taxes her sanity, so I don't think we get to see her at her best,” Watterson once explained. “I regret that the strip mostly shows her impatient side, but I try to hint at other aspects of her personality and her interests by what she's doing when Calvin barges in.”

Calvin’s mom can be just as funny as his dad, and it usually comes when the strip shows her impatient side. So to show her a bit of the respect that is so well deserved, we’ve decided to track down her best ever quote from the comic strip, and share a bit more of what’s so great about her along the way.

articles.title: 10 Perfectly Written High Fantasy Books for Fans of Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones
articles.summary: George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire proved that high fantasy doesn’t have to be synonymous with high magic. Most people in the Seven Kingdoms don’t expect to meet a dragon or giant, making it all the more terrifying when those mythical creatures appear.
body: J.R.R. Tolkien effectively established the genre of high fantasy when he came up with the world of Middle-earth and populated it with fantastical creatures facing an apocalyptic threat in The Lord of the Rings. While numerous stories introduce talking animals, fairies, or demons to a version of the real world — or even see regular people stepping into a magical realm they previously didn’t know existed — high fantasy takes place in a fully imaginary reality with its own rules, history, and factions.

One of the true masters of the genre, Ursula K. Le Guin both drew upon and subverted the classic tropes of fantasy stories. Ged, a young boy with great magical potential, has to grapple with his own impatience and hubris rather than a dark lord. The story of a boy sent to wizarding school set the stage for Harry Potter, but A Wizard of Earthsea is a far more thoughtful tale as Ged is constantly tempted by great power but must learn to avoid easy shortcuts in order to maintain balance in himself and the world. It’s an extremely quick read, so pick up the rest of the five-book series for more beautiful and meditative stories.

You had Sony with its Tobey Maguire-led Spider-Man franchise and the now-defunct 20th Century Studios with the X-Men films, Mark Steven Johnson's Daredevil movie, and the first few stabs at a Fantastic Four franchise. Even Lionsgate and New Line got in on the action with a pair of Punisher films and the Blade trilogy, respectively.

Then there was Universal, which burst onto the modern superhero scene with Lee's Hulk, starring Eric Bana, Jennifer Connelly, Sam Elliott, and Nick Nolte amongst a slew of others. In an era where the traditionally vibrant X-Men were reduced to black leather suits and both Blade and Ghost Rider ended up far more grounded than longtime comic readers would expect, Hulk pushed the boundaries of the era and it's something that still resonates more than two decades later.

articles.title: The people of video games on what gives them cause for hope
articles.summary: Hello and welcome to one of our final pieces for Optimism Week here on Eurogamer. This time, we've turned to the industry itself for some answers, and as such I'm going to do my best to get out of the way as quickly as possible.
body: For this piece, we contacted a range of developers and general people-of-video-games to ask them one question: despite everything, what still gives you reason for optimism?
"It's a rough time for the games industry but a golden age for the game dev community.

"I've seen a tremendous outpouring of support for people after layoffs and for new writers trying to break in. It's moving to see the way people rally around their colleagues to raise money, find jobs, offer feedback on resumes and portfolios.

We game devs have always looked out for each other - passing the hat in hard times and mentoring new writers. But now, there's a renewed sense of responsibility and empathy for our colleagues. That feeling, that shared care and desire to help each other out, that's how we win. And it gives me hope for our future."

articles.title: "I want to keep pouring my energy into game creation going forward" - Hideo Kojima still wants to make games even at 63
articles.summary: Hideo Kojima - known as the director of the Death Stranding and Metal Gear Solid series - celebrated his 63rd birthday recently. Don't worry though, he's not interested in retiring just yet.
body: In a big post made to X, Kojima shared his thoughts on his career moving forward alongside a video of the Lumens statue in the Kojima Productions office. He wrote: "I've turned 63. As the years pile on, the things I 'must do' and the things I 'want to do' just keep multiplying. At the same time, the 'time I have available' keeps shrinking. I need to constantly scrutinize how I spend my time and how I live my life (my way of being).

"That said, once I've shouldered a burden, I can't just leave it behind. This year marks the 40th anniversary since I first started making games. It's also the 10th anniversary of founding Kojipro. From late October through the end of the year, we're planning to hold the 'Kojipro Exhibition,' at the Azabudai Hills Gallery. Even the entrance Ludens has been updated to the '10th Anniversary Ludens' version. Amid all sorts of opportunities and offers coming my way, I want to keep pouring my energy into game creation going forward. Looking forward to your continued support."
points: Hideo Kojima - known as the director of the Death Stranding and Metal Gear Solid series - celebrated his 63rd birthday recently.
